clue.text: Strengthen the door thus and run away

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: fit a sliding bar to a door to make it secure
second meaning: the idiom for dashing off to escape

explanation.surface: Someone reinforces a door and then flees, as if both were tasks on a security checklist.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the idiom taken literally: a bolt is a door fastening, and 'it' is the door.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to flee suddenly, as a horse bolts; literally it describes fitting a fastening to something.

clue.text: Uncertain substitutes for tennis event

parts.note: mixed feelings are uncertain ones
a double stands in for an actor, a substitute

explanation.surface: Unreliable replacement players are brought in for a tennis competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed doubles is the tennis competition in which each side is a pair of one man and one woman.

clue.text: Australian climber conveys knockout in a specific way

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
the French phrase à la means in the manner or style of

explanation.surface: A mountaineer from Australia delivers a knockout blow in some particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a tree-climbing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is a tree-dwelling marsupial native to Australia that spends its life up eucalyptus trees.

clue.text: Tea chest I constructed is in good taste

indicators.note: something constructed is put together from parts, so these letters are assembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter's tea chest turns out to be a tasteful piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic describes something pleasing in appearance, showing refined artistic judgement and style.

clue.text: Individual looked like Cyclops

parts.note: a single individual is one
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A lone person gazed like the giant of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclops of Greek myth was a giant with a single eye in the middle of his forehead.

clue.text: Forces tailless thrush to pick up stone

indicators.note: picking something up means holding it, so the shortened bird takes the other piece inside it
without a tail means the bird's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the songbird, taken as written
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A songbird missing its tail is made to lift a pebble, as birds do with snails.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone goes inside the shortened bird, before its last letter. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust is to push forcefully, so the verb thrusts means the same as forces or shoves.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant in reserve

parts.note: the figure zero, nothing, looks like the letter O
a synonym

explanation.surface: Having nothing pleasant kept back for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans kept on ice are put aside and held for later use, as food is kept chilled until needed.

clue.text: In general, promises to be bright

parts.note: taken as written
Gen is the abbreviation for the military rank of General
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Speaking broadly, the outlook promises to be sunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as one phrase meaning broadly, but its two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright idea or person is clever and inventive, which is what ingenious means.

clue.text: Kiss Raymond's photographs

parts.note: X is the kiss written at the end of a letter
Ray is short for Raymond, with the possessive kept

explanation.surface: Someone kisses the snapshots belonging to a man called Raymond.
explanation.definitionFit: X-rays are images of the inside of the body, taken as photographs on radiographic film.

clue.text: Yearnings, after a year has gone, for income

indicators.note: something that has gone is missing, so one letter is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Longings for a bigger salary, once a year has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money someone is paid for work, their income.

clue.text: Heat tripe and ham hash in the stadium

indicators.note: a hash is a jumbled dish of chopped ingredients, so the preceding words are chopped up and mixed

parts.note: the letters of heat, tripe and ham, with 'and' only joining them

explanation.surface: Instructions for warming a meaty fry-up at a sports ground's food stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hash' sounds like another ingredient in the recipe; it is the signal to mix the letters. Tripe is cow's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an open arena with tiered seating all round, like a Roman stadium.

clue.text: The lady becomes pale

indicators.note: the words turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged to form a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman loses her colour, as if after a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathly pallor is the ghastly whiteness of a corpse, so deathly can describe a pale complexion.

clue.text: Sea bird breaks whole bone

indicators.note: the bird breaks into the other word, splitting it open and sitting inside

parts.note: a sum is a whole amount, a total
a tern is a gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird fractures an entire bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whole bone' reads as a phrase, but 'whole' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum, or breastbone, is the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Love role's abstract style

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
an actor's role is their part

explanation.surface: A romantic part in a play is written in a non-realistic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s movement of abstract paintings using geometric patterns to create optical illusions.

clue.text: Assailant splatters grass with gore

indicators.note: splattering scatters things messily, so the letters are spread about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An attacker leaves blood spattered over the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is the one who attacks first, an assailant in a fight or war.

clue.text: Kitchen help makes recipe set hard

parts.note: a recipe produces a dish
blood or cream sets when it clots
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A kitchen assistant prepares a dish that sets solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen help' suggests a person, but the help is a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is the cloth used for washing and wiping plates, a humble aid in the kitchen.

clue.text: Old political reformers sit up breaking records

indicators.note: the short word breaks into the longer one and sits inside it

parts.note: charts are records, as of a ship's course or a patient's progress

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Veteran campaigners rise from their seats and smash records.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a British working-class movement of the 1830s and 1840s demanding votes for all men.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartists campaigned for the People's Charter, a programme of electoral reform in nineteenth-century Britain.

clue.text: Cinema makes grown-up blind

parts.note: a grown-up is big, as children say
a window blind screens out light

explanation.surface: Watching films renders an adult sightless.
explanation.definitionFit: The big screen is an idiom for the cinema, as opposed to the small screen of television.

clue.text: Bit of potato was hot? Nonsense!

parts.note: the eye of a potato is the bud from which it sprouts
taken as written
H is the label for hot on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a chip of potato was hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for rubbish or claptrap, talk meant to deceive rather than inform.

clue.text: Yellow bread needs biting

parts.note: nan, or naan, is a flat Indian bread
a keen or biting wind is sharp and cold

explanation.surface: A yellowish loaf requires chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth from Nanjing, and the name also means its pale buff-yellow colour.

clue.text: A Hardy heroine returned to get a benefit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the heroine's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's best-known heroine

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy character comes back to collect a payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective meaning tough; it is the novelist Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful or valuable, an advantage or benefit to whoever has it.

clue.text: Contemplate rambling rose getting blight

parts.note: to eye something is to look at and consider it

indicators.note: rambling means wandering off course, so the flower's letters stray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener studies a climbing rose that has caught a plant disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling rose' is a real climbing variety, so 'rambling' hides as part of the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight that spoils a place, just as a blight mars a landscape.

clue.text: Get French and German agreement to set up a kind of board

parts.note: oui is French for yes
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Diplomats need French and German consent before establishing a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreement' serves both languages: a French yes followed by a German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ouija board is a lettered board used at seances, supposedly to spell out messages from spirits.

clue.text: A foolish person can't sue when injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An idiot finds that a lawsuit is impossible after getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is informal slang for someone crazy or silly, a fool.

clue.text: Found in spare napkin ring

indicators.note: the letters are found sitting inside the following words, across the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: Something turned up inside a spare serviette holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Napkin ring' reads as one object; 'ring' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is an enclosed space for contests, like a boxing ring or circus ring, as an arena is.

clue.text: Guess at state I'm in after early start

indicators.note: after says the larger piece follows the single letter rather than coming first
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: the short word goes in, so it sits inside the word just before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone speculates about the condition they are in after rising early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State I'm in' reads as a phrase about one's condition, but it puts one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate something is to judge its size or value roughly, to make a reasoned guess at it.

clue.text: Perfume is dispatched by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by how it sounds means a word spoken out loud stands for one spelt differently

parts.note: dispatched means sent off, as a parcel is

explanation.surface: A bottle of perfume has apparently been posted.
explanation.definitionFit: Scent is a pleasant smell, and also the bottled fragrance people wear, perfume.

clue.text: Pause with each strap being twisted

indicators.note: something twisted is wrenched out of shape, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rest break is taken while every harness strap gets twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short respite, a chance to rest or think before carrying on.
